Alberto Besozzi received the **MDPI Best Poster Award** at the 3rd edition of the *International Summer School on Wearable Sensors*, held at Università Campus Bio-Medico di Roma on 8–10 June 2026. The award, sponsored by *Applied Sciences* — an open-access journal published by MDPI — was assigned by the school's Scientific Committee to the poster receiving the highest overall evaluation.

The winning poster, **MYRA-TECH: Myopia Risk Assessment TECHnologies**, presents an ergonomic head-worn device for continuously monitoring a child's visual environment. It combines multichannel spectrometers for ambient light spectrum and intensity, an 8×8 time-of-flight sensor and an RGB camera for measuring viewing distances at high spatial resolution, and an inertial measurement unit for activity classification — all battery powered, for a full day of measurement.
